summary.headline: BCL Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore (10.5% margin) despite revenue falling to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue fell to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore, mainly due to closure of the edible oil unit and exit from packaged oil. EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore, with margin up 370 bps to 10.5%, and PAT rose 6% to INR 36 crore (5.7% margin). Distillery EBITDA margin improved to 12.41%, while ENA realisations fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. A fire at a 200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol tank on 19 June 2026 shut that plant temporarily; management said insurance recovery is virtually certain and no net loss was booked. Management also completed the acquisition of the remaining 25% of Svaksha Distillery and reduced working capital borrowings, but deferred the Fatehabad 250 KLPD project and the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project.

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 12.41% in Q1 FY27 versus 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26. ENA volume rose to 19,376 KL from 7,960 KL YoY, but ENA realisation fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. The 115 TPH paddy straw boiler meets 100% of steam and power needs.

segments.name: Country liquor (PML)
segments.commentary: Sold 6,37,993 boxes, up 42% QoQ and 46% YoY. Punjab Raspberry launched in Q4 FY26 and Jamun Vodka in July 2026. Management targets 30 lakh cases this year out of a market of about 1.25 crore cases per annum in Punjab.

segments.name: Edible oil / packaged oil (exited)
segments.commentary: Exit completed, including closure of the Bathinda oil and vanaspati unit. Soft oil refinery and trading continue as legacy operations. Revenue decline was mainly from this exit.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the 200 KLPD Bathinda plant to restart in about 15 days from the call, and that the new 150 KLPD Bathinda unit (commissioned in early July 2026) will substantially offset the lost volume.
Order book described as full for about the next three months, supported by OMC allocation of about 4.5 crore litres from a Supreme Court order covering until November.
Management guided to a sustained distillery/overall margin range of about 10% to 12%, while noting raw material and fuel price volatility.
Working capital limit to be reduced by INR 50 crore in August 2026; management aims to bring working capital utilisation towards zero over about 1.5 years.
No share buyback planned for now. Debt will rise only if a new capex project is started.
capex_capacity: Svaksha Distillery (350 KLPD, Kharagpur, West Bengal) became wholly owned on 30 June 2026 after the remaining 25% stake was acquired.
Newly added 150 KLPD Bathinda unit began commercial trials at end-June 2026 and was commissioned in the first half of July 2026.
200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol plant shut after the 19 June 2026 fire; the tank was holding about 90,000 litres at the time and is under repair.
Fatehabad 250 KLPD grain-based plant: orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash; machinery orders are reportedly finalised and management is waiting before starting construction.
Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project is on hold because biodiesel prices are not remunerative. Goyal Distillery 250 KLPD project is on hold pending industry clarity.
Malt plant is at conceptualisation stage with no timeline. IMFL entry targeted for next year, with the company still working on it.
Bio-CBG is under active evaluation (Haryana policy noted), with paddy straw feedstock seen as tricky. The company is not making biodiesel.
demand_pricing: ENA and private ethanol supply face price pressure from oversupply. Average private ethanol price is about INR 58/litre ex-factory, mainly to Reliance.

Management said maize-based ethanol to OMCs is profitable, while FCI-rice-based ethanol is near cost. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same. Blended average EBITDA is about 12%, roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA.
Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter. Current maize price is about INR 25/kg, and management said ENA prices have been revised upwards.
DDGS prices have eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for both maize and rice based.
Management expects ethanol demand to improve only slightly next year, as sugarcane-based ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel demand is a long-term driver, with few FFV models on sale so far.
Management said E20 is in place for about 18 months with no major vehicle damage seen, but blending expansion beyond E20 may be delayed. Isobutanol and SAF are cited as future demand sources.
